sentences.en: Last summer, despite his better judgment, Brian Vance found himself in a situation that, unfortunately, many of us have been in.
sentences.zh: 去年夏天，布莱恩·万斯在违背理智的情况下，不幸陷入了我们许多人都曾经历过的一种境地。

sentences.en: An argument with some random person on Reddit.
sentences.zh: 和Reddit上的某个陌生人吵了一架。

sentences.en: Which is probably not the best thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这大概不是什么明智之举。

sentences.en: You know, getting into online fights is not a good use of anyone's time, and it's definitely not good for your blood pressure.
sentences.zh: 你知道，卷入网络争吵既浪费时间，也绝对不利于血压健康。

sentences.en: Brian is a journalist based in Portland, Oregon, who founded something called Stumptown Savings.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩是一位常驻俄勒冈州波特兰市的记者，他创办了一个名为“树墩城储蓄”的网站。

sentences.en: That is frequent 99PI contributor, Will Aspinall.
sentences.zh: 那位是《99%隐形》的常客，威尔·阿斯皮纳尔。

sentences.en: Stumptown Savings is a website that covers local grocery deals.
sentences.zh: “树墩城储蓄”是一个涵盖当地杂货店优惠信息的网站。

sentences.en: Every Thursday, Brian releases a newsletter where he helps his readers find the best food prices in the area.
sentences.zh: 每周四，布莱恩都会发布一份时事通讯，帮助读者寻找该地区最实惠的食品价格。

sentences.en: He read me a little snippet.
sentences.zh: 他给我读了一小段内容。
食品储藏室，截止至8月19日。

sentences.en: Equal Exchange chocolate bar, select varieties, $3.99 each.
sentences.zh: Equal Exchange巧克力棒，指定品种，每块3.99美元。

sentences.en: Annie's Organic Salad Dressing, select varieties, $2.99 each.
sentences.zh: Annie's有机沙拉酱，指定品种，每瓶2.99美元。

sentences.en: You can see this is pretty dry.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出这内容相当枯燥。

sentences.en: Like, there's not a lot that I can do to make it intriguing to read.
sentences.zh: 就是说，我没法把它写得引人入胜。

sentences.en: Once again, Organic Peanut Butter, select varieties, $5.99 each.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，有机花生酱，指定品种，每罐5.99美元。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I'm not under the guise that I'm going to win, like, a Pulitzer Prize in literature for this.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我的意思是，我并不指望靠这个去赢得什么文学普利策奖。

sentences.en: It mightn't be Faulkner, but Brian takes a lot of pride in his work,
sentences.zh: 这可能算不上福克纳的作品，但布莱恩对自己的工作引以为豪，

sentences.en: including visiting grocery stores in person to find the hottest deals for his readers.
sentences.zh: 包括亲自去杂货店为读者寻找最热门的折扣。

sentences.en: Stumptown Savings has become my full-time job.
sentences.zh: “树墩城储蓄”已经成了我的全职工作。

sentences.en: Like, I spend 40 hours a week doing this.
sentences.zh: 我每周花40个小时做这件事。

sentences.en: Just trying to help people, like, have some say, have some power in what feels like a powerless struggle with,
sentences.zh: 只是想帮助人们，让他们在面对看似无力的抗争时，能有一些话语权，有一些力量，

sentences.en: you know, corporate greed and inflation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对抗企业贪婪和通货膨胀。

sentences.en: As you can tell, Brian puts a lot of effort into Stumptown Savings,
sentences.zh: 如你所见，布莱恩在“树墩城储蓄”上投入了大量心血，

sentences.en: so he was particularly miffed when a user on Reddit accused him of the ultimate sin,
sentences.zh: 所以当Reddit上的一位用户指责他犯了终极罪行时，他感到特别恼火，

sentences.en: using ChatGPT to compose his newsletter.
sentences.zh: 那就是用ChatGPT来撰写他的时事通讯。

sentences.en: Brian didn't use AI, but it wasn't just the accusation itself that he found offensive.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩并没有使用人工智能，但他感到被冒犯的不仅仅是这个指控本身。

sentences.en: It was the evidence the Reddit user provided to support his allegation.
sentences.zh: 而是那位Reddit用户用来支持其指控的证据。

sentences.en: A Reddit user accused me of using AI, pointing to my use of, quote,
sentences.zh: 一位Reddit用户指责我使用人工智能，并指出我使用了，引用，

sentences.en: extra-long emdashes that are not possible to replicate on a normal keyboard, end quote.
sentences.zh: “普通键盘无法打出的超长破折号”，引用结束。

sentences.en: So anyone who uses an emdash must be using AI, and that's just not the case.
sentences.zh: 所以，任何使用破折号的人一定都在使用人工智能，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: The reason why this Redditor believed Brian was using AI was because he chose to use an emdash.
sentences.zh: 那位Reddit用户之所以认为布莱恩在使用人工智能，是因为他选择了使用破折号。

sentences.en: The emdash, if you're not familiar, is a form of punctuation that looks like a horizontal bar in a sentence.
sentences.zh: 如果你不熟悉的话，破折号是一种标点符号，看起来像句子中的一条横杠。

sentences.en: It gets its name from its size, which is about the width of a capital M.
sentences.zh: 它的名字来源于它的长度，大约是一个大写字母M的宽度。

sentences.en: Not to be confused with the hyphen or its persnickety cousin, the emdash,
sentences.zh: 不要把它和连字符或它那挑剔的表亲混淆，破折号，

sentences.en: emdashes are incredibly versatile because they can replace commas, colons, semicolons, and parentheses.
sentences.zh: 破折号非常通用，因为它们可以代替逗号、冒号、分号和括号。

sentences.en: It's an odd thing to be a fan of an emdash, but I am a fan of it.
sentences.zh: 成为破折号的粉丝是一件奇怪的事，但我确实是它的粉丝。

sentences.en: It's a fun piece of punctuation.
sentences.zh: 这是一种有趣的标点符号。

sentences.en: There's a group of people who understand it and appreciate it and really value its flexibility.
sentences.zh: 有一群人理解它、欣赏它，并真正重视它的灵活性。

sentences.en: Today, there are many diehard fans of the emdash, but humans aren't the only ones who have taken to using the mark.
sentences.zh: 如今，破折号有很多死忠粉，但人类并不是唯一使用这种符号的群体。

sentences.en: Recently, large language models like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini have been sprinkling M's in their responses like digital confetti.
sentences.zh: 最近，像ChatGPT、Claude和Gemini这样的大型语言模型一直在它们的回答中像数字五彩纸屑一样散布着M型破折号。

sentences.en: There are some people who look at it and be like, well, an AI must have did this because why would a human use an emdash?
sentences.zh: 有些人看到它会说，嗯，这一定是人工智能干的，因为人类为什么要用破折号呢？

sentences.en: But, you know, that's, I'm a human.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，那是，我是一个人类。

sentences.en: I can confirm I'm a human.
sentences.zh: 我可以确认我是一个人类。

sentences.en: Today, we're reclaiming the emdash for Brian and other humans.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要为布莱恩和其他人类正名，夺回破折号的使用权。

sentences.en: Because this plucky bit of punctuation has had a very, very long literary history, way beyond today's tussles with technology.
sentences.zh: 因为这种勇敢的标点符号有着非常、非常悠久的文学历史，远不止今天与技术的这些纠葛。

sentences.en: It's been on a hero's journey, playing the lead in an adventure story that has spanned both centuries and the pages of our most beloved plays, novels, and poeMs.
sentences.zh: 它经历了一场英雄之旅，在一部跨越了几个世纪，出现在我们最钟爱的戏剧、小说和诗歌页码中的冒险故事里担任主角。

sentences.en: The emdash's origins can be found in trying to find an elegant answer to a very old problem.
sentences.zh: 破折号的起源可以追溯到人们试图为一个非常古老的问题寻找优雅的答案。

sentences.en: The problem that existed was that there wasn't really a good set of rules for punctuating text.
sentences.zh: 当时存在的问题是，对于文本标点，并没有一套真正好的规则。

sentences.en: There wasn't really any kind of convention that persisted for all that long or that was usable across lots of different contexts.
sentences.zh: 并没有任何一种惯例能够持久存在，或者在许多不同的语境中通用。

sentences.en: This is Keith Houston, author of the book Shady Characters, The Secret Life of Punctuation, Symbols, and Other Typographical Marks.
sentences.zh: 这位是基思·休斯顿，《阴暗角色：标点符号、符号和其他排版标记的秘密生活》一书的作者。

sentences.en: He says that while punctuation crept into writing systems around the 3rd century BCE,
sentences.zh: 他说，虽然标点符号在公元前3世纪左右潜入书写系统，

sentences.en: the rules that governed them remained both complex and inconsistent well into the 11th and 12th centuries.
sentences.zh: 但管理它们的规则在11和12世纪之前一直既复杂又不一致。

sentences.en: It was around that time an Italian scholar decided to leave his mark on the world of punctuation.
sentences.zh: 大约在那个时候，一位意大利学者决定在标点符号的世界里留下自己的印记。

sentences.en: His name was Bon Compagno da Signia.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫邦·孔帕尼奥·达·西尼亚。

sentences.en: But we're mercifully going to call him Bonnie.
sentences.zh: 但我们还是仁慈地叫他邦尼吧。

sentences.en: He practiced something called Ars Dictiminis, which was the formal art of composing letters in official documents.
sentences.zh: 他实践着一种叫做“书信艺术”的东西，这是在官方文件中撰写信件的正式艺术。

sentences.en: The problem was that he found the then system of punctuation not up to snuff for his letter writing.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，他发现当时的标点系统对于他的写信需求来说不够好。

sentences.en: So he came up with his own.
sentences.zh: 于是他想出了自己的一套。

sentences.en: And so when you had someone like Bonnie deciding to write a guide to letter writing,
sentences.zh: 所以当像邦尼这样的人决定编写一本写信指南时，

sentences.en: it was kind of up to him to decide how to punctuate things.
sentences.zh: 如何给事物加标点符号在某种程度上就由他来决定了。

sentences.en: And for whatever reason, he chose this very simple system.
sentences.zh: 不管出于什么原因，他选择了这个非常简单的系统。
邦尼创造了两个标点符号。

sentences.en: One he called Vergula Sursum Erecta, which looked like a forward slash.
sentences.zh: 一个他称之为“直立逗号”，看起来像一个正斜杠。

sentences.en: That one indicated a pause in a sentence.
sentences.zh: 那个符号表示句子中的停顿。

sentences.en: The forward slash was eventually shortened and dropped to the bottom of the line,
sentences.zh: 正斜杠最终被缩短并降到了行底，

sentences.en: transforming it into the comma we all recognize today.
sentences.zh: 把它变成了我们今天都认识的逗号。

sentences.en: It remains his greatest contribution to punctuation.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是他对标点符号最大的贡献。

sentences.en: And if you're fluent in Italian, which I am not, you will know that Vergola means comma.
sentences.zh: 如果你精通意大利语，而我不精通，你会知道“Vergola”的意思就是逗号。

sentences.en: He also created a second mark called Vergula Plana, which was a horizontal dash that ended the sentence, like a period.
sentences.zh: 他还创造了第二个符号，叫做“平逗号”，那是一条横杠，用来结束句子，就像句号一样。

sentences.en: And that is like a flat dash or a horizontal dash that looks exactly like a modern N or M dash.
sentences.zh: 那就像是一条平坦的横杠，或者看起来和现代的N型或M型破折号完全一样的横杠。

sentences.en: But using a dash at the end of a sentence did not catch on.
sentences.zh: 但在句末使用破折号并没有流行起来。

sentences.en: And for several centuries, it was difficult to find consistent uses of the dash.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几个世纪里，很难找到破折号的一致用法。

sentences.en: Possibly because the dash was not widely adopted, its grammatical role remained slightly unclear and therefore malleable.
sentences.zh: 可能是因为破折号没有被广泛采用，它的语法作用仍然有些模糊，因此具有可塑性。

sentences.en: I don't think it's entirely unreasonable to look at the marks around it.
sentences.zh: 我认为审视它周围的符号并不是完全不合理的。

sentences.en: So the full stop or period, the question mark, the comma, the colon, the semicolon.
sentences.zh: 比如句号、问号、逗号、冒号、分号。

sentences.en: And to a certain extent, they were all not fixed, but in slightly more common use.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，它们都不是固定的，但使用得稍微普遍一些。

sentences.en: Whereas the dash seemed to have, yeah, slid into this new era of printing without necessarily a big weight of opinion behind it.
sentences.zh: 而破折号似乎，是的，滑入了印刷的新时代，却不一定有强大的舆论支持。

sentences.en: So perhaps it seemed more flexible.
sentences.zh: 所以也许它看起来更灵活。

sentences.en: There was freedom to experiment in its use, which is exactly what happened when it got mixed up in the theatrical milieu of 16th and 17th century Elizabethan England.
sentences.zh: 它的使用有实验的自由，这正是当它混入16和17世纪伊丽莎白时代英国的戏剧环境时所发生的情况。
不，你们这些不自然的巫婆。

sentences.en: I will have such revenges on you both that all the world shall.
sentences.zh: 我要对你们俩进行报复，让全世界都……

sentences.en: What they are yet I know not, but they shall be the terrors of the earth.
sentences.zh: 那是什么我还不知道，但它们将是地球的恐怖。

sentences.en: There's a technique in theatre called apossiopisis, which is an ancient Greek term for speech that is deliberately broken off mid-sentence.
sentences.zh: 戏剧中有一种技巧叫“中断法”，这是一个古希腊术语，指故意在句子中间中断的演讲。

sentences.en: Used sparingly, it can add dramatic effect to dialogue.
sentences.zh: 适度使用，可以为对话增加戏剧效果。

sentences.en: Playwrights use the dash in writing to indicate thinking pauses, interruptions, mid-speech realisations or changes of subject for their actors.
sentences.zh: 剧作家在写作中使用破折号来表示演员的思考停顿、打断、演讲中的突然领悟或话题转换。

sentences.en: Shakespeare's first folio is a really good example where people are cut off when they lose their train of thought.
sentences.zh: 莎士比亚的第一对开本是一个很好的例子，人们在失去思路时会被打断。

sentences.en: It uses quite a lot of dashes.
sentences.zh: 它使用了相当多的破折号。

sentences.en: I think because it gives a bit of flexibility, it gets a bit more expressiveness than, you know, full stops and commas and colons and so on.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为它提供了一点灵活性，比句号、逗号、冒号等等更能表达情感。

sentences.en: Are they informed of this, my breath and blood fiery, the fiery duke till the hot duke that, no but not yet, maybe he is not well.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这件事吗，我的呼吸和血液火热，火热的公爵直到那热情的公爵，不，但还没，也许他不太舒服。

sentences.en: King Lear, as performed by Sir John Gielgud in 1994.
sentences.zh: 《李尔王》，由约翰·吉尔古德爵士于1994年表演。

sentences.en: A character facing the demons of old age, bad decisions and ungrateful children.
sentences.zh: 一个面对老年、错误决定和不孝子女恶魔的角色。

sentences.en: In other words, someone who might get lost in his thoughts more than moSt.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，一个可能比大多数人更容易迷失在思绪中的人。

sentences.en: Using dashes to show a passio pieces has remained a staple of stage writing.
sentences.zh: 使用破折号来表现中断法一直是舞台写作的主食。

sentences.en: But around 100 years after Shakespeare, in the early 18th century, an emerging branch of the literary arts elevated it from mere stage direction to a featured performer.
sentences.zh: 但在莎士比亚之后大约100年，即18世纪初，文学艺术的一个新兴分支将其从单纯的舞台指导提升为特色表演者。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I guess if playwrights had used the dash to imply how a speaker was performing these words, I suppose, for novelists, it was also used to indicate how someone,
sentences.zh: 是的，所以我猜如果剧作家使用破折号来暗示说话者是如何表演这些台词的，我想，对于小说家来说，它也被用来表示某人，

sentences.en: the cadence of how someone was speaking, to try and bring that to life a little bit.
sentences.zh: 某人说话的节奏，试图让它变得生动一点。

sentences.en: The novel as a literary form was, well, novel.
sentences.zh: 作为一种文学形式的小说，嗯，是新颖的。

sentences.en: It was a brand new form of writing, with stylistic conventions that broke away from classical rules of literature.
sentences.zh: 这是一种全新的写作形式，其风格惯例打破了古典文学规则。

sentences.en: Writers at the time explored authentic fictional characters with complex inner thoughts and naturalistic ways of speaking.
sentences.zh: 当时的作家探索了具有复杂内心思想和自然说话方式的真实虚构人物。

sentences.en: And the M-dash was how early novelists attempted to capture that.
sentences.zh: 而破折号就是早期小说家试图捕捉这一点的方式。

sentences.en: The dash became a really handy device to create the sense of someone almost dictating their adventures onto the page.
sentences.zh: 破折号成为了一种非常方便的工具，可以营造出一种仿佛有人在将他们的冒险经历口述到纸上的感觉。

sentences.en: Nowhere is this more obvious than a rambling, satirical novel called Tristram Shandy, written by Lawrence Stern in 1759.
sentences.zh: 这一点在1759年由劳伦斯·斯特恩撰写的一部漫谈式讽刺小说《项狄传》中表现得最为明显。

sentences.en: With us, you see, the case is quite different.
sentences.zh: 你看，对我们来说，情况完全不同。

sentences.en: We are all ups and downs in this matter.
sentences.zh: 在这件事上我们都有起有落。

sentences.en: Or tis fifty to one, sir, that you are a great dunce and a blockhead.
sentences.zh: 或者有五十比一的可能，先生，你是个伟大的笨蛋和傻瓜。

sentences.en: Not that there is a total want of intermediate steps.
sentences.zh: 并不是说完全缺乏中间步骤。

sentences.en: We're not so irregular as that comes to.
sentences.zh: 我们还没到那么不规则的地步。

sentences.en: But the two extremes are more common, and in a greater degree, in this unsettled island.
sentences.zh: 但这两个极端在这个动荡的岛屿上更为常见，程度也更深。

sentences.en: This short excerpt has seven dashes in it, and it's used in every which way.
sentences.zh: 这段简短的摘录中有七个破折号，而且它的用法多种多样。

sentences.en: In its wayward, dash-drewed madness, it feels like Tristram Shandy is a fully rounded and totally flawed human being.
sentences.zh: 在它任性、充满破折号的疯狂中，感觉《项狄传》的主人公是一个完全圆满且完全有缺陷的人。

sentences.en: There had been nothing like it before in English literature.
sentences.zh: 在英国文学史上，此前从未有过这样的作品。

sentences.en: You know, someone like Stern, when he's writing Tristram Shandy, he's jumping in and out of thoughts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，像斯特恩这样的人，在写《项狄传》时，他的思绪跳进跳出。

sentences.en: He's trying to commit this almost stream of consciousness narrative to paper, and it feels like it could have been written yesterday.
sentences.zh: 他试图将这种近乎意识流的叙事写在纸上，感觉它就像是昨天写的一样。

sentences.en: I don't know what it is.
There's something about the verve, the gusto behind it.
sentences.zh: 它背后有一种活力，一种热情。

sentences.en: It must have been like a bolt from the blue.
sentences.zh: 那一定像晴天霹雳一样。

sentences.en: It must have been so incredible for people at the time to read this.
sentences.zh: 当时的人们读到这个一定觉得太不可思议了。
但小说家们并没有就此止步。

sentences.en: Another way they used the dash to convey the illusion of reality was by using the dash to censor sensitive content.
sentences.zh: 他们使用破折号来传达现实幻觉的另一种方式是使用破折号来审查敏感内容。

sentences.en: It wasn't just for sort of the sake of prurience.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是为了那种猎奇的目的。

sentences.en: It was also to give a sense of authenticity, I think, to sort of titillate the readers a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是为了赋予一种真实感，去稍微挑逗一下读者。

sentences.en: In a world dominated by non-fiction, these early writers were using every trick in the book to be taken seriously
sentences.zh: 在一个由非虚构作品主导的世界里，这些早期作家使用了书中的每一个技巧来被认真对待，

sentences.en: and make their make-believe stories feel believable.
sentences.zh: 并使他们的虚构故事感觉可信。

sentences.en: One of the ways they did this was by writing as if the fictional narrative actually took place.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做的方法之一是写得好像虚构的叙事真的发生过一样。

sentences.en: Novels were commonly written in the first person as if they were letters, diary entries, or memoirs
sentences.zh: 小说通常以第一人称书写，就像它们是信件、日记条目或回忆录一样，
